Q: Keras Loss from multiple model outputs A:

The case where you have a separate loss function for each output layer is described in The Functional API Guide:

When compiling this model, you can assign different losses to each output. You can even assign different weights to each loss – to modulate their contribution to the total training loss.

model.compile(
    optimizer=keras.optimizers.RMSprop(1e-3),
    loss=[
        keras.losses.BinaryCrossentropy(from_logits=True),
        keras.losses.CategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=True),
    ],
    loss_weights=[1.0, 0.2],
)

Since the output layers have different names, you could also specify the losses and loss weights with the corresponding layer names:

model.compile(
    optimizer=keras.optimizers.RMSprop(1e-3),
    loss={
        "priority": keras.losses.BinaryCrossentropy(from_logits=True),
        "department": keras.losses.CategoricalCrossentropy(from_logits=True),
    },
    loss_weights={"priority": 1.0, "department": 0.2},
)

Train the model by passing lists of NumPy arrays of inputs and targets:

# Dummy input data
title_data = np.random.randint(num_words, size=(1280, 12))
body_data = np.random.randint(num_words, size=(1280, 100))
tags_data = np.random.randint(2, size=(1280, num_tags)).astype("float32")

# Dummy target data
priority_targets = np.random.random(size=(1280, 1))
dept_targets = np.random.randint(2, size=(1280, num_departments))

model.fit(
    {"title": title_data, "body": body_data, "tags": tags_data},
    {"priority": priority_targets, "department": dept_targets},
    epochs=2,
    batch_size=32,
)

Q: Could not install openpyx1 in window 10 A: 
import pandas as pd
from openpyxl import Workbook
from openpyxl.chart import BarChart, LineChart, Reference

# داده‌های فنی
tech_data = {
    'Parameter': ['Q (kW)', 'LMTD (°C)', 'A (m²)', 'Number of Tubes', 'Tube Length (m)', 'Shell Diameter (approx, m)'],
    'Value': [2380.84, 24.82, 112.83, 191, 7.51, 0.49]
}
tech_df = pd.DataFrame(tech_data)

# داده‌های اقتصادی
econ_data = {
    'Parameter': ['Total Investment (USD)', 'Annual Maintenance (USD)', 'Annual Savings (USD)', 'Net Annual Cashflow (USD)', 'Payback Period (years)', 'NPV (USD)', 'IRR (%)', 'B/C Ratio'],
    'Value': [3417.5, 136.7, 38400.0, 38263.3, 0.09, 188617.15, 1119.63, 56.19]
}
econ_df = pd.DataFrame(econ_data)

# ایجاد workbook
wb = Workbook()

# شیت فنی
ws_tech = wb.active
ws_tech.title = "Technical"
for r in tech_df.itertuples(index=False):
    ws_tech.append(tuple(r))

# اضافه کردن نمودار خطی به شیت فنی
line_chart = LineChart()
line_chart.title = "Technical Parameters"
line_chart.style = 12
line_chart.y_axis.title = "Value"
line_chart.x_axis.title = "Parameter"

data = Reference(ws_tech, min_col=2, min_row=1, max_col=2, max_row=len(tech_df) + 1)
cats = Reference(ws_tech, min_col=1, min_row=2, max_row=len(tech_df) + 1)
line_chart.add_data(data, titles_from_data=True)
line_chart.set_categories(cats)
ws_tech.add_chart(line_chart, "D2")  # موقعیت نمودار در سلول D2

# شیت اقتصادی
ws_econ = wb.create_sheet("Economic")
for r in econ_df.itertuples(index=False):
    ws_econ.append(tuple(r))

# اضافه کردن نمودار میله‌ای به شیت اقتصادی
bar_chart = BarChart()
bar_chart.type = "col"
bar_chart.style = 10
bar_chart.title = "Economic Analysis"
bar_chart.y_axis.title = "Value (USD or %)"
bar_chart.x_axis.title = "Parameter"

data = Reference(ws_econ, min_col=2, min_row=1, max_col=2, max_row=len(econ_df) + 1)
cats = Reference(ws_econ, min_col=1, min_row=2, max_row=len(econ_df) + 1)
bar_chart.add_data(data, titles_from_data=True)
bar_chart.set_categories(cats)
ws_econ.add_chart(bar_chart, "D2")  # موقعیت نمودار در سلول D2

# ذخیره فایل
wb.save('project_analysis_with_charts.xlsx')
print("فایل اکسل با نمودارها ساخته شد: project_analysis_with_charts.xlsx")

Q: Is @Async method outside transaction? A:

As autext already says, the @Async causes the code to run in a different thread. Since the async method can end after the calling method, using the same transaction would require that transaction to remain active until the async method completes as well. Since that is (almost) never what you want, the async method does not inherit the transaction.

is @Async removing changes the process or not?

It does, but how much depends on the exact code inside the async method. Removing the annotation makes the calling method wait until it finishes. That means that the method can take longer; how much longer depends on the async method. But another big change is that any exception thrown from the previously-async method will now find its way into the calling method. If you don't handle it, it could lead to a transaction rollback (depends on the exception type), but it will definitely lead to error responses (if this is called from a REST handler).
